claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by competition between configurational entropy and atomic-scale lattice distortion.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion dictates the formation of stable phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Phase formation or stability influences high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Changing the alloy composition, particularly the relative amounts of Cr and Fe versus Co and Ni, will alter the proposed governing competition.
Cr and Fe are elements that contribute to lattice distortion in this alloy system.
Co and Ni enhance configurational entropy in this alloy system.
Composition and thermal processing affect atomic-scale lattice distortion and short-range order.
Competition between configurational entropy and lattice-distortion energy influences phase separation.
Competition between configurational entropy and lattice-distortion energy influences precipitation.
Competition between configurational entropy and lattice-distortion energy influences the formation of stable phases.
Optimizing phase stability will improve high-temperature strength.
Optimizing phase stability will improve environmental resistance.
Optimizing phase stability will improve radiation tolerance.
Optimizing phase stability will improve cryogenic toughness.
Grain-boundary effects and impurities may also influence phase stability.
